answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an economy requires each agent to anchor identity registration at a verification wharf by submitting a cryptographic stake burning transaction. Burning tokens destroys value permanently, leaving only an ember of burned proof. The cost scaling function enforces a steep ridge: burning expenses scale superlinearly as $C(n) = k \cdot n^{1.5}$ or exponentially with the number of registered identities $n$, making mass replica creation economically fatal.
